course.title: Email Forensics
course.description: A standards-aware, practical course on acquiring, preserving, parsing, reconstructing, correlating, and reporting email evidence. It covers Internet email architecture, RFC 5322 structure, MIME, routing and Received fields, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, Authentication-Results, EML/MSG/PST/MBOX artifacts, attachment and URL triage, Python automation, timelines, hosted-mail trace and audit evidence, incident-response integration, and a complete defensive capstone.
prerequisites: Basic networking concepts including IP, DNS, and client/server communication
Python fundamentals are recommended for automation lessons
learningOutcomes: Explain how Internet email moves through submission, SMTP relays, DNS, gateways, and mailbox systems.
Differentiate SMTP envelope identities from RFC 5322 message headers.
Parse raw .eml evidence with Python's standards-aware email package.
Interpret RFC 5322 headers, Message-ID relationships, Received fields, and MIME structures.
Reconstruct mail paths and normalize timestamps while documenting uncertainty.
Interpret SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Authentication-Results without confusing domain authentication with human attribution.
Explain the forensic roles and limitations of EML, MSG, PST, and MBOX artifacts.
Extract and hash attachments and URLs without executing or visiting suspicious content.
Automate repeatable email evidence processing and produce structured reports.
Correlate message evidence with provider trace, audit, endpoint, identity, and DNS records.
Construct source-preserving timelines and evidence relationships.
Write professional findings that distinguish observations, inference, confidence, and limitations.
Complete an authorized end-to-end email-forensics investigation.

modules.title: Forensic Foundations and Evidence Handling
modules.description: Establish the forensic mindset: scope, authority, preservation, hashing, provenance, chain of custody, and the limits of email evidence.

lessons.title: What Email Forensics Can Prove
lessons.description: Learn to distinguish observable message facts, receiver-generated evidence, inference, and unsupported attribution.
learningObjectives: Map common investigative questions to email evidence.

notes.text: Core idea
Email forensics reconstructs events from preserved message artifacts and related records. A visible From field is a claim in the message; it is not by itself proof that a person authored the message.

items: Use recipient-side evidence when reconstructing delivery.
Treat IP addresses as infrastructure clues, not human identities.
Corroborate strong conclusions with independent records.

notes.text: Never convert a header clue directly into a human attribution without independent evidence.

quiz.question: What does a From field establish by itself?
quiz.explanation: RFC 5322 defines From as an originator field; it is not a human identity proof.

practicals.title: Hash an evidence file
practicals.description: Create a reproducible manifest for a laboratory .eml file.
steps: Place a lab .eml file under evidence/.
Recalculate the hash and compare it.
practicals.solution:
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, json
from datetime import datetime, timezone

p = Path("evidence/sample.eml")
digest = hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
manifest = {
    "evidence_id": "EF-LAB-001",
    "filename": p.name,
    "size_bytes": p.stat().st_size,
    "sha256": digest,
    "recorded_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
}
Path("manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
practicals.output: The manifest contains the actual file size and SHA-256 digest; unchanged bytes produce the same digest.

from pathlib import Path

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone

tasks.title: Reconstruct a Mail Transport Path
tasks.description: Build a hop table from Received fields and a laboratory MX snapshot.
tasks.problemStatement: Normalize timestamps; preserve raw fields; identify uncertainty.
tasks.hint: Analyze Received fields from the recipient side and retain raw values.
tasks.solutionCode:
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
import json

msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parse(open("message.eml", "rb"))
hops = []
for index, value in enumerate(msg.get_all("Received", []), start=1):
    stamp = None
    if ";" in value:
        try:
            stamp = parsedate_to_datetime(value.rsplit(";", 1)[1].strip()).isoformat()
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            stamp = "UNPARSED"
    hops.append({"header_position": index, "timestamp": stamp, "raw": value})

print(json.dumps({"received_hops": hops}, indent=2))
tasks.solutionExplanation: The solution keeps raw trace data and only normalizes timestamps when parsing succeeds.

practicals.title: Parse a raw message
practicals.description: Inventory key headers and parser defects.
practicals.solution:
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from pathlib import Path

raw = Path("message.eml").read_bytes()
msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(raw)

for name in ["From", "To", "Date", "Subject", "Message-ID"]:
    print(name, ":", msg.get(name))
print("defects:", [type(x).__name__ for x in msg.defects])
practicals.output: The output reports actual parsed fields and parser-level defects.

quiz.question: What separates headers from the body?
quiz.explanation: RFC 5322 defines the header/body separation as an empty line.

summary: Preserve raw bytes and parse standards-aware.

lessons.title: MIME and Attachments
lessons.description: Understand multipart boundaries, content types, transfer encodings, nested messages, and attachment extraction.

notes.text: MIME is representation
MIME describes how message content is divided and encoded. Base64 is a transfer encoding, not authentication or malware detection.

practicals.title: Extract and hash attachments
practicals.description: Create a metadata and SHA-256 inventory.
steps: Write them to an analysis directory.
practicals.solution:
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, json

msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parse(open("message.eml", "rb"))
out = Path("attachments"); out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
records = []
for idx, part in enumerate(msg.walk()):
    filename = part.get_filename()
    data = part.get_payload(decode=True)
    if not filename or data is None:
        continue
    target = out / f"{idx:03d}_{Path(filename).name}"
    target.write_bytes(data)
    records.append({
        "filename": filename,
        "content_type": part.get_content_type(),
        "size": len(data),
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
        "path": str(target)
    })
Path("attachments.json").write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps(records, indent=2))
practicals.output: The inventory ties decoded bytes to their source filename, MIME type, and hash.

quiz.question: What is base64 in MIME primarily?
quiz.explanation: Content-transfer-encoding describes representation during transport.

tasks.title: Build a MIME Evidence Inventory
tasks.description: Generate a JSON inventory of MIME parts and extracted attachment hashes.
tasks.problemStatement: Record MIME index, type, filename, size, hash, and extraction path.
tasks.hint: Use part.walk(), get_filename(), get_payload(decode=True), and hashlib.
tasks.solutionCode:
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json

message_path = Path("message.eml")
message = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(message_path.read_bytes())
inventory = []

for part_no, part in enumerate(message.walk()):
    payload = part.get_payload(decode=True)
    inventory.append({
        "part": part_no,
        "content_type": part.get_content_type(),
        "filename": part.get_filename(),
        "decoded_size": len(payload) if payload is not None else None,
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() if payload is not None else None
    })

Path("mime_inventory.json").write_text(
    json.dumps(inventory, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),
    encoding="utf-8"
)
print("parts:", len(inventory))
tasks.solutionExplanation: The solution produces a machine-readable attachment inventory and does not execute content.

lessons.title: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, Authentication-Results
lessons.description: Interpret SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Authentication-Results without overstating what they prove. The DMARC standards were updated in May 2026: RFC 9989 defines the core DMARC protocol and RFC 9990/9991 cover aggregate and failure reporting; these replace RFC 7489.
learningObjectives: Explain DMARC alignment at a high level.
Interpret Authentication-Results within a trust boundary.

notes.text: Distinct roles

items: SPF evaluates authorization for an SMTP envelope identity.
DKIM cryptographically associates selected message data with a signing domain.
DMARC evaluates alignment between authenticated identifiers and the visible From domain and applies policy.
notes.text: SPF evaluates authorization for an SMTP envelope identity against DNS policy. DKIM cryptographically associates selected message data with a signing domain. Current DMARC is defined by RFC 9989, with aggregate reporting in RFC 9990 and failure reporting in RFC 9991. These mechanisms are valuable but do not, by themselves, establish the physical human who authored a message.
A DKIM pass is not proof that a particular human authored the message.

quiz.question: What does DKIM primarily provide?
options: A verifiable association with a signing domain
quiz.answer: A verifiable association with a signing domain
quiz.explanation: DKIM provides a cryptographic signing-domain association.

summary: Authentication is domain/system evidence, not automatic human attribution.

lessons.title: Header Forgery and Trust Boundaries
lessons.description: Separate sender-controlled fields from receiver-generated evidence.
learningObjectives: Explain why trusted receiver evidence matters.

items: From and Subject are message claims.
Received is normally added by transport systems.
Authentication-Results has value when inserted by a trusted receiver.

notes.text: Correlate headers with provider logs and preserve the receiving trust boundary in the report.

quiz.question: Why does Authentication-Results require a trust boundary?
options: A sender can construct a header with that name
quiz.answer: A sender can construct a header with that name
quiz.explanation: Header names alone do not establish provenance.

summary: Provenance matters as much as field content.

tasks.title: Classify a Suspicious Header
tasks.description: Produce an evidence matrix for sender claims, routing, and authentication results.
tasks.problemStatement: Separate observations, confidence, and unresolved attribution.
tasks.solutionCode:
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser

message = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parse(open("suspicious.eml", "rb"))
matrix = [
    ("From", str(message.get("From")), "sender-controlled claim"),
    ("Return-Path", str(message.get("Return-Path")), "envelope-related evidence if preserved"),
    ("Authentication-Results", message.get_all("Authentication-Results", []), "receiver-reported result; trust boundary required"),
    ("DKIM-Signature", message.get_all("DKIM-Signature", []), "cryptographic signing evidence"),
    ("Received", message.get_all("Received", []), "transport trace evidence")
]
for field, value, interpretation in matrix:
    print(field, "=>", value)
    print("  interpretation:", interpretation)
tasks.solutionExplanation: The solution gathers evidence but deliberately leaves interpretation to the analyst.

tasks.problemStatement: Produce hashes, MIME metadata, URL strings, indicators, and recommended next action.
tasks.hint: Indicators are reasons for review, not proof of maliciousness.
tasks.solutionCode:
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json

rows = []
for path in sorted(Path("attachments").iterdir()):
    if not path.is_file():
        continue
    data = path.read_bytes()
    rows.append({
        "artifact": path.name,
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
        "size_bytes": len(data),
        "triage_status": "analyst_review",
        "reason": "Static evidence recorded; execution not performed."
    })

Path("triage.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
print("triaged:", len(rows))

notes.title: Merge event records
notes.description: Sort message and provider JSON events by UTC.
notes.solution:
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

events = []
for name in ["message_events.json", "provider_events.json"]:
    for e in json.loads(Path(name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(e["event_time_utc"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        e["parsed"] = dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)
        events.append(e)
for e in sorted(events, key=lambda x: x["parsed"]):
    print(e["parsed"].isoformat(), e.get("source"), e.get("event_type"))
notes.output: The timeline is a derived view; source events remain intact.

tasks.title: Automate an Email Case Summary
tasks.description: Build a standard-library-only case summarizer for multiple .eml files.
tasks.problemStatement: Hash messages, inventory headers, hash attachments, preserve Received fields, and write deterministic JSON.
tasks.hint: Hash source bytes before parsing and sort filenames for deterministic output.
tasks.solutionCode:
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, json

def summarize(path: Path):
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(raw)
    return {
        "file": path.name,
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        "message_id": msg.get("Message-ID"),
        "received_count": len(msg.get_all("Received", [])),
        "attachment_names": [p.get_filename() for p in msg.walk() if p.get_filename()],
        "defects": [type(d).__name__ for d in msg.defects]
    }

case = Path("case")
result = [summarize(p) for p in sorted(case.glob("*.eml"))]
Path("case_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
print("case messages:", len(result))
tasks.solutionExplanation: The workflow is offline, source-preserving, and deterministic.

# Email Forensics Case Laboratory
Use only authorized laboratory evidence. The workflow is offline: it parses `.eml` files, hashes source and attachment bytes, inventories headers/MIME structure, and correlates optional JSON records. It does not execute attachments or visit URLs.
code.email_forensics.py:
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, hashlib, json
from datetime import timezone
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from pathlib import Path

def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

def parse_timestamp(value: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not value:
        return None
    try:
        dt = parsedate_to_datetime(value)
        if dt is None or dt.tzinfo is None:
            return "UNPARSED"
        return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return "UNPARSED"

def analyze_message(path: Path, outdir: Path) -> dict:
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(raw)
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    attachments = []
    for index, part in enumerate(msg.walk()):
        filename = part.get_filename()
        data = part.get_payload(decode=True)
        if not filename or data is None:
            continue
        target = outdir / f"{index:03d}_{Path(filename).name}"
        target.write_bytes(data)
        attachments.append({
            "part_index": index,
            "filename": filename,
            "content_type": part.get_content_type(),
            "size_bytes": len(data),
            "sha256": sha256_bytes(data),
            "path": str(target)
        })
    return {
        "file": path.name,
        "sha256": sha256_bytes(raw),
        "size_bytes": len(raw),
        "headers": {
            "From": str(msg.get("From")) if msg.get("From") else None,
            "To": str(msg.get("To")) if msg.get("To") else None,
            "Subject": str(msg.get("Subject")) if msg.get("Subject") else None,
            "Date": str(msg.get("Date")) if msg.get("Date") else None,
            "Date_UTC": parse_timestamp(msg.get("Date")),
            "Message-ID": str(msg.get("Message-ID")) if msg.get("Message-ID") else None,
            "Authentication-Results": msg.get_all("Authentication-Results", []),
            "DKIM-Signature": msg.get_all("DKIM-Signature", []),
            "Received": msg.get_all("Received", [])
        },
        "mime_parts": sum(1 for _ in msg.walk()),
        "attachments": attachments,
        "parser_defects": [type(x).__name__ for x in msg.defects]
    }

def load_records(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return [value]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return value
    raise ValueError(f"{path} must contain an object or array")

def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Offline email-forensics case analyzer")
    parser.add_argument("case_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("case_report.json"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    messages = args.case_dir / "messages"
    extracts = args.case_dir / "extracted_attachments"
    reports = [analyze_message(p, extracts) for p in sorted(messages.glob("*.eml"))]
    external = []
    for name in ("trace.json", "audit.json", "endpoint.json"):
        external.extend(load_records(args.case_dir / "provider" / name))
    report = {
        "message_count": len(reports),
        "messages": reports,
        "provider_records": external,
        "method_notes": [
            "Source bytes are hashed before parsing.",
            "Attachments are decoded and hashed but never executed.",
            "No network requests are made."
        ]
    }
    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

project.explanation: The architecture treats source messages as preserved evidence and every parsed result as a derived view. Source bytes are hashed before parsing. Attachments are extracted only for static analysis and are never executed. URL extraction is offline. Provider records remain separate source objects. Authentication fields are reported for analyst interpretation rather than converted into an automatic verdict. The final report should contain scope, evidence inventory, methods, findings, timeline, artifact analysis, limitations, conclusion, and reproducibility notes.
